findings.title: The Judiciary did not require independent approval of purchases less than $2,500. Consequently, one Clerk employee circumvented the Judiciary’s procurement policies including the purchase approximately $438,600 in office supplies from a vendor that did not have a contract with the Judiciary and at higher cost than the Judiciary’s existing office supply contract.
findings.description: The Judiciary lacked independent approval for purchases under $2,500, totaling $3.4 million during the audit period. One employee circumvented policy by processing over $1 million in transactions, including nearly $439,000 to an uncontracted vendor at higher costs than existing contracts.
findings.recommendation: establish procedures for independent review of all transactions including those below $2,500; take corrective action, including disciplinary action, for improper transactions; and ensure existing contracts are used for the purchase of goods and services.

extraction.agency_response_summary: The Judiciary agrees with all recommendations but notes existing procedures require independent approval for transactions under competitive thresholds via Express Purchase Orders (XPO). They plan to implement an annual review process and monitor spending activities to ensure compliance, with completion dates marked as ongoing.
